title: Runtime Telemetry Annotator (scratchpad)
content:
Context / quick motivation:
- We need a tiny, low-latency component that can attach lightweight semantic annotations to runtime events (ingress/egress/kv-cache hits, model-variant selection, batching decisions) without blowing up p99 or adding heavy dependency on central processing.
- Goal: make traces and metrics richer for cost attribution, fallback-forensics, and quick root-cause surfaces, while preserving PII/privacy and keeping storage/query cheap.

Scope (what this sketch covers):
- API shape for an "annotator" shim that runs in the request path (or as a sync sidecar) and enriches event payloads.
- Sampling policy primitives and heuristics for adaptive trace enrichment.
- Minimal on-wire JSON proto examples and a suggested internal compact binary tag format for storage.
- Privacy/PII masking rules and opt-out semantics.

Non-goals:
- Full distributed tracing system design (we leverage existing tracing backend).
- Large-batch offline enrichment.

Constraints / assumptions:
- The annotator must add < 1ms median latency on typical requests and < 3ms p99 for lightweight annotation path (configurable to be async for heavy annotations).
- Runs co-located with runtime process or as a tiny sidecar process that shares a unix socket.
- Event envelope size budget: ~1KB additional bytes for annotated metadata on average; must be configurable.

Design primitives:
1) Annotation record = {key, value, confidence, tier, ttl}
   - key: short string (dash-separated), value: short string (or numeric), confidence: low|med|high, tier: e.g., telemetry|forensics|cost, ttl: seconds (how long to retain this annotation in caches)
2) Annotations are idempotent by key. Newer annotations with higher confidence override older ones.
3) Attachments: small blobs (e.g., normalized prompt tokens fingerprint) allowed only when tier==forensics and sampling allowed.
4) Tag compression: server-side compacts tags into index ids before storage to save bytes.

API shape (HTTP/JSON example, minimal):
POST /v1/annotate
Headers:
  - X-Req-ID: <request id>
  - X-Inject-Mode: sync|async|best-effort  # hint for latency-sensitive calls
Body: {
  "req_id": "r_123",
  "phase": "ingress",
  "observed": {"model": "gpt-7x-unopt", "seq_len": 32, "route": "route-a"},
  "annotations": [
    {"k": "kv-cache-hit", "v": "true", "confidence": "high", "tier": "cost", "ttl": "300"},
    {"k": "prefetchable", "v": "yes", "confidence": "med", "tier": "telemetry", "ttl": "60"}
  ]
}
Response (sync): {"status":"ok","applied": ["kv-cache-hit"]}
Notes: The runtime may emit pre-populated candidate annotations; annotator validates, augments, and returns applied-list. When X-Inject-Mode==async, server returns 202 immediately and annotator attempts async enrichment (best-effort).

Compact storage serialization (internal):
- Represent annotation entries as colon-separated short tokens: "kc:1:3" where kc is key-code, 1 is value-code, 3 is confidence-level. Server maintains per-cluster dictionary.
- Store dictionaries in tiered caches (L1 ephemeral, L2 long-lived) to avoid repeated string writes.

Sampling & trigger rules:
- Base sampling rate per-route (0.1% default) + priority overrides: can force-sample for errors, high-cost requests (> token threshold), or manual on-demand via admin API.
- Adaptive sampling: if anomaly detector flags high variance in per-token latency or cost, increase sampling for recent tenants/routes.
- Deterministic reservoir sampling: keep one annotated example per N requests per tenant per minute to ensure representative coverage.

Privacy / masking rules (must be pluggable):
- Default: redact any free-text fields that match phone/email/SSN heuristics. Replace with stable hash (salted per-tenant) for correlation.
- For forensic-tier attachments: require explicit canary flag and higher sampling thresholds plus approval (audit log).
- Expose tenant-level opt-out via token scope; annotator enforces quickly.

Operational behaviors / failure modes:
- Fast-path (annotate in-process): synchronous, small annotations only. If annotator fails, fallback to no-annotation path and increment internal metric.
- Async path: write to ephemeral queue (bounded), if queue full, drop oldest best-effort annotations (emit dropped counter).
- Backpressure: if annotation pipeline is slow, auto-switch routes to async.

Example enrichments we want for dashboards / RCA:
- cost.unit = "tokens"; cost.variant = "quant4x"; model.selection.reason = "fallback-latency"; batch.size=4; kv.cache.miss_reason = "stale-prefix"
- These should be short tokens for queryable counts and to drive attribution joins against usage logs.

Query patterns we must support (hints for storage):
- Count annotations per route/model per hour (cost analytics)
- Look up last N annotated requests for a given tenant+route with filters (forensics)
- Join annotations to trace spans by req_id for aggregated dashboards

Migration notes (from existing span-enrichment work):
- Keep compatibility layer: annotator can piggyback on existing span proto but strip heavy payloads.
- Start with a single cluster-level dictionary and migrate to per-tenant when space/time permits.

ASCII flow diagram (simplified):

Client ---> Ingress Edge ---> Runtime (request) ---[sync annotate]---> Annotator (in-proc or sidecar) ---> trace/metric pipeline
                                        |--[async enqueue]--> annotator-queue --> worker --> storage/backend

Open questions / TODOs:
- Rate-limit semantics per-tenant for annotations: should we bill or throttle? (billing impact)
- How to version the annotation dictionary without global coordination? (proposal: rolling epoch ids in header)
- Compact encoding: protobuf vs custom short-token scheme tradeoffs (benchmark CPU and memory).
- Should confidence be numeric (0-100) rather than low/med/high for more expressivity?
- What are SLO knobs to guarantee annotator not hurting p99 under noisy garbage collection or heavy CPU?

Next actions (short-term):
- Quick prototype: in-process annotator that implements POST /v1/annotate, sample-based, and compacts to proto. Benchmark median/p99 overhead on small QPS toy (owner: Aisha). Due: 2025-06-27.
- Add tenant opt-out header support and unit tests for masking heuristics (owner: Priya). Due: 2025-07-04.
- RFC draft for dictionary epoch header and on-disk compaction strategy (owner: Ethan). Due: 2025-07-08.

Notes to self: keep API minimal, prefer extensible key-value short tokens. Preserve ability to escalate to "forensics mode" (higher sample, richer blobs) when debugging incidents.

--- end scratchpad ---
